chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad al-Halby, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those whom your right hands possess,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is specific to men, not women.' I said, 'So do women seek permission during these three times?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but they enter and exit. And those who have not yet reached puberty from you?' He said: 'From yourselves.' He said: 'Upon you is seeking permission like the permission of those who have reached puberty during these three times.'

key_terms.الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ: Those whom your right hands possess (concubines/slaves)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on seeking permission for women and children according to Quran 33:58?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of Quran 33:58, specifying that the strict etiquette of seeking permission during the three times of privacy (morning, noon, and night) applies to men and pre-pubescent boys, while women are exempt from this formality. It further extends the requirement to young boys who have not yet reached puberty, aligning with the Shia interpretation that 'those who have not reached puberty among you' refers to males, thereby establishing a gender-specific distinction in domestic privacy norms.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad Al Halby, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [33:55] what their right hands possess, heasws said: ‘It is particularly regarding the men besides the women’. I said, ‘So the women should seek permission during these three times?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but they can enter and exit, and the ones who have yet to attain puberty from you. From yourselves, it is upon you that you seek permission like the permission of the ones who have reached puberty during these three times’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from Muhammad al-Halabiy from Zurarah who has said the following:

“This is about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . those whom your right hands possess’ [24:58] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is just for men and not for women.’ I then asked, ‘Is it then necessary for women to ask permission in such hours?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, they can come and go.’ About, ‘. . . those who have not gained feeling of carnal desire,’ [24:58] he (the Imam) said, ‘It is a reference to yourselves (free people).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must ask for permission, like those who have become mature, during the three hours.’”
